how: Your attendance score starts at 100. Late clock-ins, missed shifts and giving away a shift with under 24 hours’ notice lower it; picking up shifts raises it. It climbs back with good attendance (on-time shifts, streaks, 30 days with nothing counted, commendations), older deductions fade, and your organization may also restart it once a year. Every change is listed on your file.
Sick days and protected leave never count. A supervisor can excuse anything else with a reason, and the reason stays visible to you.
Supervisors can add notes about your work, including commendations. You're notified each time and see exactly what they wrote.

The score and notes only help managers notice when a conversation may help. Nothing schedules, disciplines or ends your employment automatically; a person decides, and you can always respond in writing.
Every time a manager opens your file, it's logged. You can ask HR to correct anything inaccurate, and you have a right to see the information held about you.

privacyNotice.title: Your privacy
privacyNotice.intro: What this app keeps about you, why, who can see it, and what you can ask for. Your employer is responsible for your information; FlexcityHeadquarters is the tool it uses.

collect.title: What’s kept, and why
items: Who you are and how to reach you: name, work email, phone, language, employee number.
Your work: positions, certifications, availability, schedule, time off and leave balances.
Your time: clock-in and clock-out times, and corrections with the reason, for pay.

Pay, if your employer pays you through the app: pay rate, tax claim amounts (TD1), deductions, your bank account (sealed) and Social Insurance Number (sealed), and your home mailing address for tax slips.
HR files about you: reviews, training, onboarding items, attendance events, conduct notes, discipline, accommodations and injury claims, and documents you or HR upload. Medical notes are HR-only.

see.title: Who can see it
items: You can see your own file, pay statements and documents.
Your supervisor sees what they need to run your department: your schedule, time, availability and the records they wrote. Not your medical information, pay details or banking.
HR sees your full file. Payroll sees pay and tax details, with banking and SIN masked.
Colleagues see your first name and last initial on your department's published schedule.
FlexcityHeadquarters staff can't see employee records. If your employer asks for help, a support visit is read-only, time-limited, logged, and never opens individual records.

monitoring.title: Electronic monitoring
items: Clocking in checks once that you're at the facility. Only whether you were on site and how far away is kept, never where you were or your device's address.

Working-alone check-ins record when you check in. Your location is shared only if you turn sharing on for that session: then the app sends it about every 30 seconds while it's open on your screen, and with each check-in or help request. Only the people who monitor lone workers see it. Turning sharing off removes it at once; otherwise it's removed 30 days after the session. Nothing is shared outside a working-alone session.
Changes to records are logged (who changed what, when). Sign-ins are logged to protect your account.

Notifications on your phone are optional and can be turned off on each device. Their text is encrypted for your device; the lock screen shows only a short heading, never details about pay, health, discipline or documents.

Nothing else is tracked: no location outside a working-alone session you started, browsing, keystrokes, screenshots, camera or microphone. Attendance figures are advisory: no decision about you is made by the software alone.

keep.title: How long it’s kept
items: Pay records: the years your employer must keep them for tax (at least six after the year).
In-app notifications: 2 years by default; the email log: 90 days, and it never holds the email's contents.
When you leave, your file is kept for your employer's legal retention period, then anonymized.

Each organization's data is walled off by the database itself.
Passkeys and multi-factor sign-in; sensitive actions ask you to confirm it's you.

rules.FED: Federally regulated: a holiday with pay on another day, the working day before or after for the six fixed-date holidays (Canada Labour Code ss. 193, 195).
rules.BC: British Columbia: an average day’s pay whether or not the holiday is their day off; another day off only by written agreement (ESA ss. 44, 45, 48).
rules.AB: Alberta: nothing is owed when the holiday isn’t their normal work day and they don’t work it (Employment Standards Code ss. 27–28). You may give more.
rules.SK: Saskatchewan: public holiday pay (5% of the 4 weeks’ wages) for every holiday, whatever their days of work (Saskatchewan Employment Act s. 2-32).
rules.MB: Manitoba: their next working day off with general holiday pay, or another day you agree on (Employment Standards Code).
rules.ON: Ontario: a substitute day off with public holiday pay, or public holiday pay alone if they agree in writing (ESA s. 27).
rules.QC: Quebec: the holiday indemnity, or a compensatory day off at the employer’s choice (Act respecting labour standards ss. 62–65).
rules.NB: New Brunswick: another day off with regular pay, or a day’s regular pay instead (Employment Standards Act s. 18).
rules.NS: Nova Scotia: a day off with pay on the next working day or another day agreed (Labour Standards Code). Remembrance Day: nothing when it falls on their day off (Remembrance Day Act).
rules.PE: Prince Edward Island: another day off with pay, usually their next working day (Employment Standards Act).
rules.NL: Newfoundland and Labrador: another day off with the same pay, usually their next working day (Labour Standards Act).
rules.YT: Yukon: a holiday with pay on their next working day (Employment Standards Act).
rules.NT: Northwest Territories: holiday pay, or another day off with pay at a time you agree on (Employment Standards Act).
rules.NU: Nunavut: a holiday with pay on their next working day (Labour Standards Act).
